title: Longer-Lasting Haircuts: Everyday Care Tips for Norwich
description: Practical, easy-to-follow tips to keep your haircut looking sharp between barber visits, including daily habits, product advice and quick at‑home tweaks.

content.heading: Daily habits that protect your cut
paragraphs: Small daily choices make a big difference. Sleep on a clean, smooth pillowcase (silk or a soft cotton helps), avoid going to bed with soaking‑wet hair and dry your hair gently with a towel rather than rubbing vigorously.
Combing in the direction of the cut and being mindful with hats or helmets prevents unnecessary friction and keeps lines looking crisp for longer.

content.heading: Pick the right products — and use less
paragraphs: Choose lightweight, water‑based styling products for most short cuts; they’re easier to wash out and less likely to weigh hair down. A small pea‑sized amount evenly worked through the hands often does more good than piling product on.
Use dry shampoo to absorb excess oil between washes and a salt spray or light paste to refresh texture. Avoid heavy waxes or thick creams if you want a cleaner look that lasts.

content.heading: Washing, conditioning and scalp care
paragraphs: How often you wash depends on your hair type—every day can strip natural oils for some, while others need daily washes. Aim for a gentle shampoo and apply conditioner mainly to the mid‑lengths and ends to keep the top looking neat.
A cool rinse seals the cuticle and adds shine. Consider a clarifying shampoo once every fortnight if products build up, and treat any scalp issues early to avoid the cut looking untidy.

content.heading: Quick home tweaks and when to visit 3D Cutz
paragraphs: For short maintenance between visits try simple tools: a comb and small pair of scissors for trimming stray ends, or an electric trimmer to neaten the neckline. Blow‑drying into place after a wash helps set the shape for longer.

If the shape or fade starts to blend away, it’s time for a professional tidy up. For a local touch, pop in to 3D Cutz at 19 Prince of Wales Road, Norwich NR1 1BD for a maintenance cut rather than letting the style drift too far.
